## Responsibility

The product's inside: domain model (versioned documents, rules, memory map, import index, run state machine, plans), ports, and use cases. No I/O of its own; adapters arrive through ports.

## Invariants

- Every persisted file is stamped with its header [[cite: packages/core/src/domain/versioned.ts:148 | "stamp(body: z.output<S>): DocumentHeader & z.output<S> {"]].
- `stamp` refuses a body its own schema rejects, so a document that cannot be read back is never written; a use case checks what a person gave it first and answers with `USAGE`.
- A file that several processes read, change and write back (a run's `state.json`, the worktree registry, the backlog) is changed under a `FileLock`: `RunRepository.update` (also for a parent run's `children`, `RunSystemPlan`), `WorktreeRegistry.exclusive`, `MachineLeases.exclusive`; `LayoutStore.update` puts the daemon's changes in line inside its process. The work inside never takes the same lock again.
- One unreadable run never hides the others: overviews read runs through `RunRepository.loadAll` and name what they left out.
- An escalated run is not finished: it is counted apart (`countAttention`), listed by `escalatedOf`, refused by `DriveRun` (`notDrivable`), put back by `ResumeRun` with the escalating stage's loop at zero, and ended by `CloseRun` with a reason. A run that is not active has no open questions: `WorkOverview`, `inboxOf` and `RunJournal.answer` agree on that.
- A wait for a person (`RunJournal.waitFor`) ends without an answer when the run left the question's stage or ended; the drive then looks at the run again instead of waiting for ever.
- A run starts only where it can work: `InitRun` asks `CheckReadiness` and refuses through `startRefusal` (no git repository; for a worktree run, no commit or a dirty tree, unless `allowDirty`, which `Issues.start` passes on and intake always sets).
- A workflow's `preconditions` are a closed list (`domain/preconditions.ts`: `clean-tree`, `branch-ok`, `tests-green`), each decided by a readiness check when the run starts; `startRefusal` refuses on the first that does not hold and on any other name, which `lintWorkflow` rejects. `tests-green` runs the quick gate (`CheckReadiness` with `gates`), which nothing else does unasked. A human gate skipped by the run's autonomy grants what approving it grants (`skipGates`); `lintWorkflow` refuses a skippable gate that grants a push.
- Local state has no path override: `MetatorConfig` v12 dropped `paths.runs`, `index`, `discovery` and `gates`, and a config rewritten at the current version loses them (`RETIRED_CONFIG_KEYS`).
- Refactor plans and system plans share one lifecycle (`domain/plan-progress.ts`: `approvePlan`, `requireApproved`, `asDraft`, `settled`, `progressOf`): a rule about approval is changed there, once.
- `analyzeArchitecture` derives everything once (`archContext`, `domain/architecture-context.ts`) and then only reads it: violations come from the ordered `ARCH_RULES` (`architecture-rules.ts`), the report's sections from `architecture-boundaries.ts`. The whole report is pinned for four inputs (`test/architecture-characterization.test.ts`, `test/fixtures/architecture`); a new rule is one function added to the list.
- A person's edit of a plan or the map (`RunPlans`, `SystemPlans`, `SystemMaps`, ADR-0087) names the digest it was based on (`CONFLICT` otherwise), is checked by the document's schema before it is written, and is recorded with `by`: a `plan-edited` activity line, or the `<file>.edits.jsonl` log. A run's plan freezes at its approval gate (`planReadOnlyBecause`); a system plan step with a run never changes.
- Dangerous commands are one list (`guard.commands` of `MetatorConfig` v13, `domain/guard-commands.ts`): `guardCommand` gives `never`, `ask` or `allow` for an argv, `preToolPolicy` answers from it, and a host that can deny tools itself gets the same list (`denyToolsOf`). A consent in words is the person's own message only (`consentsIn`: no question, no refusal, nothing `[metator]` typed), kept by `GuardConsents` per pane or host session, valid for `guard.consentMinutes`, used once. Nothing else lets an `ask` command pass but the host's own prompt and, in a run, the run's approval (`push` covers the commit). The chat a person talks in is part of no run: `GuardPreTool` reads no active run for a pane with role `apps` and no run of its own, so a run that works in the same checkout binds neither its edits nor its commands. A pane is never a `run drive` session for the guards (`GuardSession.pane`).
- Whether a change is quick is decided without a model (`domain/quick.ts`: `quickCheck` over facts `QuickCheck` gathers from the diff, the workspace, the import graph, the API snapshots and the system map; the task's words through `taskEscalators`). `quickOverride` lets a person's sentence keep it quick, never across repositories. The two cards of a quick run are run questions asked by gate commands (`QuickFit`, `QuickReady`), recognised by `QUICK_READY_PROMPT`, `QUICK_GREW_PROMPT` and `QUICK_OPTIONS`; `Fine` ends the run in `AnswerQuestion` unless a live drive carries it, and no drive starts for it. A gate command that asks a person (`metator quick fit`, `quick ready`) says not yet with `WAITING` (exit 4): a drive polls it without spending a loop, and a conductor reads the gate script in its first message (`conductorPrompt`) and runs it with `--wait`. A run that continues another in its worktree (`InitRun` with `adopt`, a quick run continued as full) keeps the worktree's id, which is the first run's: `RunRepository.resolveId` gives the active run that adopted it once the first one ended, and `QuickFit` re-points the registry entry.
- A direct edit not meant for a commit is a `ScratchRecord` with its patch (`Scratch`, `WorkingPatches` port): taken out by reverse-applying, never forced, and remembered until the person deals with it (a record whose lines changed since stays as `changed`; it leaves only by a full drop, by `forget`, or when no file holds its lines, which `list` and `drop` say in `gone`); `Scratch.inCommit` tells the commit guard which debug files a commit would hold. Only a task's main chat (the pane with `startedRun` of the session's run or of its parent) or a person steers a session (`SessionSteering.refusal`). What is typed for the person waits in `PaneMail` until the agent is idle and never goes over a question it asked; every such line begins with `[metator]`.
- Errors cross layers as one type [[cite: packages/core/src/domain/errors.ts:26 | "export class MetatorError extends Error {"]].

## Allowed dependencies

Only the pure libraries approved in ADR-0010 (enforced by MT-ARCH-003). Never runtime, cli or plugins (MT-ARCH-002); tests may use `@metator/testing`.

## Pitfalls

- Changing a document schema in place breaks files users already have: add a version and an `upgrade` (MT-CODE-003).
- A deleted module has no node in the import graph: `ComputeAffected` finds its importers through the imports that resolve to nothing now, by relative path, by the `candidates` an alias leads to, or by the directory of a workspace package imported by name (`missingEntries`).
- A new setting is an option in the registry (`domain/option-registry.ts`), not a field of `MetatorConfig`: one definition gives the CLI, the daemon and the app its type, default, scope and description (S1).
- A document is read and written through `application/document-io.ts` (`readDocument`, `loadDocument`, `writeDocument`, `readJsonLines`, `scanDocuments`), not by parsing and stamping by hand; a reader that skips a bad file or line on purpose says so (`"skip"`). `metator.config` is changed only through `editRepoConfig` (`application/config-file.ts`): it keeps a YAML file's comments, drops the retired keys and validates the result before writing.
- A port file with a callback type (`=>`) counts as behavior for MT-TEST-003, so ports stay in `ports/index.ts` (the one file the rule exempts). `Bun` and `process` do not exist here (MT-ARCH-004); take what you need through a port.
- `CloseRun` stops the run's driver last, after the summary is written: the caller may be a child of the process it stops.
- `Panes.restore` starts host sessions and plain shells only (`isPlainShell`); a pane that ran a command stays as it ended.
- A run asked to be seen (`StartRun` with `session`, as `RunSystemPlan` asks for every child) opens as a conductor session through the `ConductorSessions` port on `conductorHost` (the host asked for when installed, else the first installed of `supervisor.hostOrder`); only when that fails (no daemon, no interactive host, the session did not start) is it driven in the background, and `noSession` and the run's activity say why (ADR-0090).
- A pane's screen is read as it is drawn: `PtyBroker` keeps a screen model per pane through the `ScreenRenderer` port (@xterm/headless in plugin-node), the sensor reads prompts from it and `readHostPrompt` gives a blocked pane's reason as one bounded line with its numbered `menu`. A pane without a run, and an agent that asked the person in words (`agentQuestionOf` on its last message; a run's pane too, with `runId`), asks through `PaneQuestions` (in memory, `p001`…), never the run journal; the supervisor and the resume line leave such a pane alone; `HostPrompts.answerPane` answers it, and a menu's choice is typed as its key (ADR-0091). A host pane whose process goes with the daemon (`pauseAll` when it stops) or that a signal ended (exit ≥ 128) is `paused`, never `ended`: its session id and last screen (saved every few seconds, `saveScreens`) are kept, `restore` resumes it in the same pane (unless `--no-restore`), and `ContinueTask` continues a whole task across repositories, its paused panes and every active run nothing carries (its conductor, else its drive). `ResumeNotices` tells a resumed conductor or worker, once and only while it is idle and no person holds the keyboard, to go on (the supervisor leaves it alone meanwhile); `ChatNotices` tells the chat a task was given in, once per event, when it is done, stops or waits for an approval. A host's permission question carries `command`, whole (ADR-0092).
- `Panes` never removes a pane by itself: `endFinished` (the daemon's sweep), `Conductor.collect` and a process exit mark it `ended` (reason, code, summary) and keep its last screen (`.metator/panes/`); only `closePane` (a person, `closeEnded`, `run close`) removes one. An ended pane is not restored; a pane started again is no longer ended.
